content: Klesha tanu karanarthah samadhi bhavanarthash cha. (The purpose of practice is to weaken the afflictions and cultivate meditative absorption).
author: Patanjali
explanation:
In the profound psychology of the Yoga Sutras, Patanjali outlines the systematic roadmap for stilling mental fluctuations into radiant, sovereign stillness.

This teaching (Klesha tanu karanarthah samadhi bhavanarthash cha. (The purp...) focuses directly on klesha and tanu. When we clear away reactive illusions and anchor ourselves in timeless principles, the mind recovers its pristine clarity and inner resilience.

True realization is never an abstract intellectual debate—it is an active discipline lived through quiet integrity and conscious presence in everyday moments.
practicalInsight: Apply this teaching on klesha today: take a deliberate pause before reacting, align your actions with quiet integrity, and refuse to let transient friction disturb your center.
reflectionPrompt: How can you embody deeper klesha and tanu in the primary challenge you are navigating right now?
